c.tagline: Cowboy heart of the Rockies - Stampede spirit and the gateway to Banff.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around C$3.80 plus per-km and per-minute charges. App-based Uber and Lyft both operate citywide and are often cheaper.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across Canada; 811 (Health Link) is Alberta's non-emergency health line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The east end of downtown around the drop-in centre and some CTrain platforms can feel uncomfortable late at night.

hood_desc: Calgary's high-rise core plus the buzzing Beltline just to the south, home to the Calgary Tower, Stephen Avenue's shops and restaurants, and the +15 indoor skywalk network; best for first-timers who want to be central and walkable.
A trendy, village-like district just across the Bow River with independent boutiques, cafes, craft-beer bars and cinemas; suits travelers who want a compact, hip neighborhood feel.

Calgary's oldest neighborhood and one of its coolest - antique shops, art galleries, live-music venues, breweries and farm-to-table restaurants along 9th Avenue SE; great for creative, indie-minded visitors.
The 'Red Mile' entertainment strip packed with bars, patios, restaurants and boutiques, spilling into leafy Mission along 4th Street SW; the go-to area for nightlife and dining.
A quieter, historic riverside neighborhood northeast of downtown with a strong local food scene, Italian roots and easy CTrain access; good for a relaxed, residential base close to the action.

water.note: Tap water is safe and high quality throughout the city.

transit.pay: Tap a contactless credit/debit card or phone, or use the My Fare mobile app or a physical Connect card, at CTrain platform machines and on buses. One adult fare is about C$3.70 and covers 90 minutes of transfers. The downtown stretch of 7th Avenue S is a free-fare zone - CTrain rides between City Hall and Downtown West/Kerby stations cost nothing.
transit.hours: CTrain runs roughly 4:30am-1am (later on weekends); frequent MAX BRT and bus routes cover the rest, with reduced late-night service.

train: Rocky Mountaineer (seasonal tourist rail to Banff and Vancouver)
bus: Red Arrow / Ebus / FlixBus (intercity to Edmonton, Banff, Red Deer)

transit.m: Route 300 BRT (Airport/City Centre) to downtown (~45 min)
Route 100 bus to McKnight-Westwinds CTrain then Blue Line downtown (~50 min)

food.name: Alberta beef steak
food.desc: Grain-finished Alberta AAA beef, dry- or wet-aged and flame-grilled; the province's signature plate and Calgary's culinary calling card.

places.name: Caesar's Steak House
places.note: Downtown fixture since 1972; 28-day-aged beef, flame-grilled, nostalgic red-leather dining room.

places.name: Hy's Steakhouse
places.note: Long-running prime-cut room known for cheese toast and old-school table service.

places.name: Vintage Chophouse
places.note: Modern chophouse with dry-aged cuts and live jazz in a converted heritage building.

food.name: Calgary ginger beef
food.desc: Crisp battered beef strips in a sweet-sticky ginger sauce, invented in Calgary's Chinatown in the 1970s and now an Alberta staple.

places.name: Silver Dragon Restaurant
places.note: Chinatown mainstay since 1966; classic Calgary ginger beef and daytime dim sum carts.

places.name: Golden Inn Restaurant
places.note: Late-night Cantonese institution locals credit with perfecting the crispy version.

places.name: U & Me Restaurant
places.note: Family-run Szechuan-Cantonese spot, generous portions and consistently crunchy ginger beef.

food.name: Bison
food.desc: Lean prairie bison served as tartare, striploin or braised short rib; a Rocky Mountain foothills tradition older than the beef industry.

places.name: Bow Valley Ranche Restaurant
places.note: 1896 ranch house in parkland; bison tartare and game dishes with local vegetables.

places.name: River Cafe
places.note: Island lodge-style room built on Canadian regional ingredients, wood-fired game and bison.

places.name: CHARCUT Roast House
places.note: Whole-animal butchery kitchen; house-cured bison charcuterie and rotisserie plates.

food.name: Alberta beef burger
food.desc: Hand-formed patties of local chuck griddled smash-style; Calgary's everyday expression of its cattle-country beef.

places.name: Boogie's Burgers
places.note: Neighbourhood diner going since the 1960s, hand-pattied Alberta beef and milkshakes.

places.name: Clive Burger
places.note: Certified-sustainable Alberta beef, single-double smash patties, fast and consistent.

places.name: National on 17th
places.note: Busy beer hall pairing an Alberta beef burger with a huge local tap list.

food.name: Saskatoon berry pie
food.desc: Prairie berry with an almond-tinged, less tart flavour than blueberry, baked into pies and crumbles across southern Alberta.

places.name: Alberta Bakery, Heritage Park
places.note: Historic-village bakery turning out saskatoon pies from period recipes.

places.name: Bow Valley Ranche Restaurant
places.note: Prairie-berry desserts on a menu built around Alberta ingredients.

places.name: Sunterra Market
places.note: Alberta family food hall; reliable saskatoon pies and tarts to take away.

food.name: Caesar cocktail
food.desc: Canada's national cocktail, invented in Calgary in 1969: vodka, Clamato, hot sauce, Worcestershire and a celery-salt rim.

places.name: Proof
places.note: Award-winning cocktail bar; serious, well-balanced takes on the hometown Caesar.

places.name: National on 10th
places.note: Loaded brunch Caesars with pickled garnishes, packed on weekend mornings.

places.name: Charbar
places.note: Simmons Building rooftop with river views and a smoky wood-grill Caesar.

food.name: Alberta craft beer
food.desc: Calgary's taprooms brew with Alberta barley and Rocky Mountain water, from pale ales to Prairie-style lagers.

places.name: Village Brewery
places.note: Community-minded brewery whose Blacksmith and Blonde are on taps citywide.

places.name: Big Rock Brewery
places.note: Alberta's original craft brewery, opened 1985; tours and a taproom at the plant.

places.name: Annex Ale Project
places.note: Small-batch taproom in the Barley Belt brewery district, easy to combine with neighbours.

landmarks: Calgary Tower
The city's defining 1968 landmark with a glass-floor observation deck offering 360-degree views of downtown and the Rocky Mountains beyond.
Peace Bridge
Santiago Calatrava's striking red helix-shaped pedestrian bridge over the Bow River, one of the most Instagrammed structures in the city.
The Bow
Calgary's tallest skyscraper, a graceful crescent-shaped glass tower that dominates and defines the downtown skyline.
Scotiabank Saddledome
The distinctive saddle-shaped hyperbolic paraboloid arena built for the 1988 Winter Olympics, an instantly recognizable piece of Calgary's skyline.
Studio Bell (National Music Centre)
An award-winning, sculptural copper-clad building housing Canada's national music museum, notable for its bold contemporary architecture.
Heritage Park Historical Village
Canada's largest living history museum, recreating a pre-1950s prairie town with vintage steam trains and paddlewheelers.
Fort Calgary
The reconstructed 1875 North-West Mounted Police outpost at the confluence of the Bow and Elbow rivers, marking the city's founding site.
Prince's Island Park
A picturesque river-island park in the heart of downtown, beloved for its towering cottonwoods and skyline backdrop.
Devonian Gardens
A lush, glass-enclosed indoor botanical garden suspended above downtown Calgary, an unexpected oasis of greenery amid the skyscrapers.
Calgary Stampede Grounds
Home to the world-famous 'Greatest Outdoor Show on Earth,' with its iconic grandstand and rodeo arena drawing over a million visitors each July.

train.note: Calgary has no scheduled passenger rail at all - VIA Rail's transcontinental Canadian runs through Edmonton and Jasper instead, several hundred kilometres north. The only trains from Calgary are the luxury Rocky Mountaineer (https://www.rockymountaineer.com/) tourist services to Banff and Vancouver, which run seasonally and are priced as a holiday rather than transport. The CTrain is urban light rail.

bus.note: No international coaches. Since Greyhound Canada shut down, the market is covered by Red Arrow (https://www.redarrow.ca/), Ebus (https://myebus.ca/), Rider Express (https://riderexpress.ca/) and FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.ca/), running to Edmonton in about 3h30, Banff in 2 hours and east toward Saskatoon and Winnipeg. Banff Airporter and Brewster Express shuttles link the airport directly with Banff and Lake Louise.

ferry.note: Calgary sits on the prairies at the foot of the Rockies with no navigable water, so there are no ferries. Rafting on the Bow River through the city is a summer recreation, not transport.

half.name: Banff National Park
half.blurb: Canada's first national park, with turquoise lakes, hot springs and peaks of the Canadian Rockies.

half.name: Kananaskis Country
half.blurb: Mountain wilderness area in the Rockies foothills with hiking trails and alpine scenery, closer than Banff.

half.name: Drumheller
half.blurb: Badlands town home to the Royal Tyrrell Museum's dinosaur fossils, dramatic eroded hoodoo rock formations and canyon scenery.

full.name: Waterton Lakes National Park
full.blurb: Remote mountain park on the US border known for wildflower meadows, glacial lakes and the historic Prince of Wales Hotel.

full.name: Dinosaur Provincial Park
full.blurb: UNESCO World Heritage badlands site holding one of the richest dinosaur fossil beds on Earth.
